coreInvariants.description: Generated maps must satisfy both border enclosure and no-double-wall rules at the same time. Do not fix an exposed floor by adding a second parallel wall next to an existing wall. Instead, trim the shape, resize an edge/corner room, or move the border so the final visible map outline is enclosed by exactly one wall/door/window layer.

packingBehavior.description: When filling a requested area with rooms from a named size band, prefer the largest valid rectangular or square room interiors that fit the band and available space. Do not create smaller fragmented rooms or extra all-wall padding when a larger valid room can fill the space cleanly.

roomResizeBehavior.description: If a requested map size cannot be cleanly filled without double walls, individual rooms on any edge or corner may shrink within their requested size band to remove excess rows or columns. This applies equally to north, south, east, and west sides. Prefer shrinking edge or corner rooms over adding all-wall padding or preserving a rectangular external silhouette.

shapeTrimBehavior.description: The final external map shape does not need to remain a perfect rectangle or square. If satisfying a requested map size creates excess rows or columns on any side that cause double walls, trim or omit those excess tiles instead of preserving the rectangle. Ragged/non-rectangular silhouettes are valid on north, south, east, or west sides when they prevent doubled walls and keep floors enclosed.

sharedWallBehavior.description: When two rooms touch, their bordering wall lines must collapse into one shared wall line. Do not create two adjacent parallel wall rows or columns between touching rooms.

outerWallBehavior.description: A room or packed room group must not create an extra parallel outer wall row or column next to an existing wall boundary. This applies to north, south, east, and west boundaries. Any outer edge should reuse the same single wall line when adjacent to another boundary instead of adding a second wall line.

wallLayerValidation.description: Wall, door, and window tiles form wall layers. A wall layer is invalid if it has another parallel wall layer immediately adjacent on the non-floor side and does not have floor on the opposite side. Door/window/wall cap protrusions are invalid when they sit directly beside another wall layer instead of forming the single enclosing boundary. Example: a row containing wall-door-wall directly above a row of wall-wall-wall is invalid unless the door has floor on both through-sides or is a valid exterior door with outside on one side and floor on the other.

borderWallBehavior.description: The visible exterior border of the generated map must always exist as wall tiles. Border wall tiles may be replaced only by valid exterior doors or windows. Ragged rows or columns may be shorter, but every exposed edge of every existing tile must be checked. Any floor tile with missing/outside space directly north, south, east, or west is invalid. If a row is shorter than the row above it, the overhanging cells in the longer row must be exterior-safe border tiles, not floors. Remove unnecessary doors or add/restore wall tiles rather than deleting border wall tiles if the room remains internally reachable.

enclosureBehavior.description: All generated floor tiles must be enclosed by the final outer wall boundary. The exterior edge of the generated room group should be wall or door tiles, not floor tiles. Internal shared wall seams must remain continuous except where intentionally replaced by a single collapsed door tile.

collapsedBoundaryFloorBehavior.description: When wall rows or columns collapse during room packing, any affected floor rows or columns must remain inside the final room or packed room group. Do not leave a free row or column of floor tiles outside the final outer wall boundary.

sharedDoorBehavior.description: When doors from adjacent rooms would occupy neighboring or overlapping positions on a shared wall, collapse them into one shared door tile in the single shared wall line.

description: Rooms are rectangular or square areas with floor interiors and wall perimeters. Room size measurements are based on interior floor tiles only. Walls add one tile around the floor area. Raggedness controls how closely the final map follows the requested external dimensions versus trimming unused space. The two hard invariants are: no double walls anywhere, and every visible external border must be wall, door, or window. Do not solve one by violating the other. Wall layers must be validated as layers, not only as individual tiles; protruding wall/door/window caps backed by another wall layer are invalid. When filling space, prefer the largest valid room interiors in the requested size band before creating smaller rooms. If a clean fit is impossible, shrink edge or corner rooms on any side within their size band before adding padding walls. Adjacent rooms may share a single wall tile line instead of creating double walls. The final exterior shape may be trimmed, ragged, or non-rectangular on any side if preserving the requested rectangular size would create double walls, but every exposed border must still be wall, door, or window. No floor tile may touch outside/missing space in any cardinal direction. Outer boundaries may not become double walls or exterior floor rows. Collapsed floor rows or columns must remain inside the final outer walls, never outside them. Internal wall seams should remain continuous except for intentional single-door openings. If two door locations would be adjacent or overlapping on a shared wall, they should merge into one door tile. Every room must have at least one door, but unnecessary doors may be removed if the room remains reachable from the interior floorplan.
